proposals.before: Hu Ying said, "Emperor Taizu laid the imperial tombs here to show his line a capital they must not abandon."
proposals.after: Hu Ying said, "Emperor Wen laid the imperial tombs here to show his line a capital they must not abandon."
proposals.reason: Chinese 文皇 is Emperor Wen (Yongle/Chengzu), not Taizu.

proposals.before: The great ministers asked the empress dowager to install the prince as heir apparent and have the Prince of Fu act as regent.
proposals.after: The great ministers asked the empress dowager to install the prince as heir apparent and have the Prince of Cheng act as regent.
proposals.reason: 郕王 is Prince of Cheng, not Fu.

proposals.before: The great ministers together asked the Empress Dowager to establish the prince as heir apparent and order the Prince of Fu to govern as regent.
proposals.after: The great ministers together asked the Empress Dowager to establish the prince as heir apparent and order the Prince of Cheng to govern as regent.
proposals.reason: 郕王 is Prince of Cheng, not Fu.

proposals.before: The next year he came to court and was kept at the Nanjing ministry of rites, soon advanced to minister.
proposals.after: The next year he came to court and was kept at the traveling-court Ministry of Rites, soon advanced to minister.
proposals.reason: 行在禮部 is the traveling-court ministry, not Nanjing.

proposals.before: Then Huang Ying, native-office prefect of Siming, memorialized asking for it.
proposals.after: Then Huang Zeng, native-office prefect of Siming, memorialized asking for it.
proposals.reason: 黃矰 is Huang Zeng; Ying is a mistranslation of 矰.

proposals.before: Between Yingzong and Jingtai the realm was in upheaval and minds were unsettled; many who held power flattered to please.
proposals.after: Between Yingzong and Jingtai the national situation was newly changed and people's hearts were watchful; many ministers who held power and handled affairs flattered to please.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'upheaval' and 'unsettled' overstate 國勢初更 and 人心觀望; the literal rendering matches the Chinese more closely.

decisions.reason: s0075 has 文皇, Emperor Wen (Yongle/Chengzu), not Taizu (太祖); the proposed Emperor Wen matches the Chinese while preserving the rest of the idiomatic sentence.
s0152 has 郕王, the Prince of Cheng; Fu (福) is unsupported, and Prince of Cheng restores the correct princely title.
The same focus unit 命郕王攝政 names the Prince of Cheng; the literal’s Prince of Fu is the same title error and the proposed Cheng fix is accurate.
s0054 has 行在禮部, the traveling-court Ministry of Rites; Nanjing (南京) is not in the Chinese, and the proposed replacement corrects that misidentification.
s0214 names 黃矰, read Huang Zeng; Ying invents a reading of 矰, and Huang Zeng restores the correct personal name.

decisions.after: Between Yingzong and Jingtai, when the realm's situation had just changed and people watched and waited, many ministers who held power and handled affairs flattered to please.
decisions.reason: 國勢初更 is a newly changed political situation, not upheaval, and 人心觀望 is wait-and-see watching, not unsettled minds; 執政任事之臣 also includes those handling affairs. The proposal rightly rejects the overstated before reading, but 'national situation was newly changed' and 'people's hearts were watchful' are stiff calques.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 國勢初更，人心觀望，執政任事之臣多阿意取容

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0005 restores Huang Zeng for 黃矰; the English name claim's Huang Ying came only from the bad idiomatic.
